articleTitle: Torque and EMF ripple reduction in brushless machines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: This contribution describes torque and EMF ripple minimisation in electrical machines with slotted iron stators. This is a problem in electronically commutated DC machines which require trapezoidal shaped output waveforms with extended plateau regions. The approaches considered here include winding distribution, slot number selection, stator and rotor skewing, pole shaping, and special lamination designs. Two design examples illustrate the application of some of the above techniques in a two phase brushless tachogenerator and a three phase brushless motor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Impulse magnetization strategies for an external rotor brushless DC motor equipped with a multipole NdFeB magnet
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: There are a number of stages during the manufacture of a brushless DC motor at which it may be possible to impulse magnetize the permanent magnets, namely: (i) component magnetization, of the magnet poles separately or of the complete multipole magnet; (ii) sub-assembly magnetization, of the assembled multipole rotor; and (iii) post-assembly magnetization, of the fully assembled motor. Here, the authors describe how, in order to aid the design optimisation of multipole magnetization systems, and eliminate fixture design by trial-and-error, an integrated CAD methodology has been developed. It involves a number of phases, the level of sophistication of the design/analysis tools increasing as the feasible design space contracts.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Permanent magnet machines with line start capabilities: their design and application
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: For some applications it is essential that a machine, excited by permanent magnets, can operate both as a synchronous motor and also has an effective induction motor characteristic for starting purposes. The author describes the design and application of these machines which are started direct online and are required to synchronise a load which may have significant inertia.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: NdFeB magnets in DC linear stepping motors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: Advantages of DC linear motors over rotary ones in most applications requiring linear drives, are numerous. Linear motors are free of chains, gears or belts and hence compact, and have no backlashes. Unlike linear AC motors these have limited travel but are more easily controllable. The magnetic field source for these motors can be chosen to be electromagnets or permanent magnets. The replacement of the electromagnets by permanent magnets is only possible because of the superior magnetic properties of the permanent magnets presently available. The author describes the construction, analysis and performance of several NdFeB field DC linear motors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sensorless position detection in permanent magnet drives
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: This presentation is concerned with a novel method of estimating rotor position from measurements of voltage and current at the terminals of an electrical machine. The method is potentially valuable in eliminating the need for a discrete position sensing element in the broad class of rotor position-switched electric drives. The estimator can be used in drives based on different types of motor e.g. switched reluctance motors or permanent magnet motors with sinusoidal or nonsinusoidal back EMF waveforms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Manufacturing aspects of small brushless DC motors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: In the recent years brushless DC motors have penetrated into several new application areas. The number of pieces being produced has increased considerably. The average number of pieces of a specific design being produced for a small motor is considerably larger than that for a large motor. Due to this difference in number of pieces and typical dimensions different technologies are used at some stages of the manufacturing process. Here, the manufacturing of small brushless DC motors of the slotted radial field type is considered by the authors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: The author looks at the historical development of magnet materials through which it can be seen that although some of their properties have been known about for well over three thousand years, it is only in the last fifty years that applications have expanded from large holding magnets, the magneto generator and the humble compass needle. The author argues that with all the current improvements in processing (including for ferrite production), the variety of production methods for the rare-earth materials, and the new materials currently under development, the variety of products from which the designer will be able to choose will continue to expand. Along with this, the cost of all these products will continue to fall, resulting in a greater use of permanent magnets and a much greater choice for the designer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: With the advances in magnet technology and the ready availability of sintered NdFeB magnets, a new series of eddy current separators has been designed and successfully launched into the nonferrous metal recycling industry. Using permanent magnet designs, operating energy levels have been reduced to less than 6 kW.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparative study of the design and development of direct drive brushed and brushless DC motors with samarium cobalt, neodymium-iron-boron and ceramic magnets
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: Permanent magnet direct drive brushed and brushless DC motors are described. The impact of the characteristics of the magnet materials on the design and performance is discussed. The design and performance characteristics of these motors with 50 mm and 150 mm outside diameters are presented and compared. Some aspects of manufacture and application are given. The conclusion is drawn that, irrespective of applications, at the present time motors with samarium cobalt magnets are preferred without any hesitation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An integrated design approach for brushless DC drive systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: Brushless DC motor drive systems are a multi-disciplinary technology, with each of the component disciplines developing rapidly. The design of a specific topology of machine is derived from equations which relate the physical dimensions, material properties,a nd supply conditions to the required performance. Whilst elementary magnetic circuit analysis techniques are generally employed to establish the likely basis of a successful design, more advanced techniques are required to aid the refinement of designs. In order to illustrate the importance of an integrated design approach, not only for brushless DC motor drives but also for other systems based on permanent magnet excited machines, a number of case studies are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Drives and control strategies for permanent magnet machines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Permanent Magnet Machines and Drives
abstract: Permanent magnet machine drives are relatively expensive with a principal merit of high performance. They also tend to be relatively small-circa 10's of kW max. These considerations effectively eliminate the thyristor and GTO from consideration. The use of a full switch has led to the common use of DC link voltage source 3 phase inverters as by far the most common circuit. Here, the use of such drive circuits for the control of PM machines is described by the author.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
